text:
incident-bot: [PAGE] Sev2 — Canary regression detected for rollout r12345 (model: redwood-llm-v2). Route: /v1/generate. Elevated 5xx rate and p95 latency on canary hosts. Paging oncall: @june (oncall).

june (oncall): acked. oncall jumping in — collecting quick triage. severity confirmed Sev2 because customer-facing errors on some accounts.

june (oncall): which regions? any correlated infra alerts?

rahul (eng-runtime): I'm seeing the canary pool (canary-eu-1) show CPU throttling on the inference pods and lots of repeated `CUDA out of memory` logs for the quantized kernel path. pulling logs now.

rahul (eng-runtime): log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:17Z ERROR inference: kv_cache_miss -> fallback path
2026-03-15T14:02:17Z WARN  runtime: kernel_select: quantized_gemm_v2 chosen
2026-03-15T14:02:18Z ERROR runtime: oom allocating 244MB @ cudaMalloc
2026-03-15T14:02:18Z ERROR http: 5xx for request id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=500
```

june (oncall): thanks. affected tenants? any customer tickets?

carla (prodops): Support counts: 7 customer errors surfaced in last 8m, mainly short L1 SLA failures. Not broad yet but visible. Notified priority customers A/C.

rahul (eng-runtime): quick metrics diff (canary vs baseline):
- p95 latency: baseline 120ms -> canary 420ms
- 5xx rate: baseline 0.2% -> canary 3.4%
- token throughput per GPU decreased ~35%

morgan (pm): are these failures causing hallucinations or wrong output, or just 5xx/latency? customers complaining about slow + errors. no semantic regressions reported yet.

eva (sre): infra checks: node memory/oom events correlate with deployment time. However control-plane health is fine. No network flaps.

june (oncall): initial hypothesis list (will track in-thread):
1) quantized kernel change in new model build causing OOM for certain sequence lengths.
2) batching config mismatch — canary used aggressive batching resulting in larger memory spikes.
3) regression in KV cache hotpath causing more recomputation.

rahul (eng-runtime): reproducing locally with canary binary + sample load — able to trigger `cudaMalloc` OOM at seq_len ~2048 when batch_size>=4 on A100-40g. Baseline model artifact doesn't OOM. This points at kernel/quantization.

rahul (eng-runtime): command I ran: `./run_infer --model redwood-llm-v2-canary --seq 2048 --bs 4 --device a100-40` produced OOM within 3 iterations.

june (oncall): ok sounds like a safe rollback makes sense for immediate mitigation. We need to confirm rollback steps and pinning checks to avoid re-rolling forward automatically.

carla (prodops): rollback plan:
1) Abort canary rollout: `redwood rollout abort r12345 --reason "canary-memory-oom-regression"`
2) Pin traffic back to stable (model-v1.9.5): `redwood route update /v1/generate --model model-v1.9.5 --weight 100`
3) Drain canary hosts and mark for debug.

ops-bot: command accepted: abort job r12345 queued by carla. Tracking id: q-67890.

june (oncall): confirm no automatic re-deploy/auto-scale will bring the canary back. Check rollout policy: `redwood rollout describe r12345`

rahul (eng-runtime): output from `redwood rollout describe r12345`:
```
rollout: r12345
model: redwood-llm-v2-canary
status: progressing
auto_promote: true
canary_policy: scale=auto, retry=2
```

rahul (eng-runtime): auto_promote=true — will set to false before aborting to avoid flapping.

carla (prodops): changing policy: `redwood rollout update r12345 --auto_promote=false` -> accepted.

ops-bot: rollback abort executed: r12345 -> aborted by carla at 2026-03-15T14:09:22Z.

ops-bot: route update applied: /v1/generate -> model=model-v1.9.5 weight=100 at 2026-03-15T14:10:03Z.

june (oncall): verifying post-rollback metrics. please share p95 and 5xx now.

rahul (eng-runtime): initial verification: p95 back to ~130ms, 5xx dropped to 0.25% over last 5m. Can confirm canary hosts are drained; logs no longer show recent `cudaMalloc` OOM.

carla (prodops): customer update sent: "We observed an error spike during a canary rollout and have rolled back to the previous stable model. We're monitoring and we'll follow up with RCA."

morgan (pm): good. We should capture exact config delta between canary and baseline for RCA. rahul, can you diff model build flags, quantization params, and kernel selection metadata?

rahul (eng-runtime): yes. preliminary diff:
- quantization profile: canary used `qtype=int8_v2` with per-channel scales, baseline `int8_v1` per-tensor
- kernel hint: canary enabled `matmul_fuse=true` in kernel selector
- memory allocator tweak: `arena_reserve=0.15` changed from 0.10

rahul (eng-runtime): putting full diff in the incident doc (will attach). Early suspicion: `matmul_fuse=true` + int8_v2 path picks an untested kernel that spikes temporary memory usage for long sequences.

june (oncall): action items (assigning in-thread):
- rahul: capture full build + deploy artifact diff + reproduce steps (timeline target: +2h)
- eva: run canary-sim stress test across seq lengths and batch sizes to map OOM boundaries (+1h)
- carla: coordinate customer comms + confirm any SLA credits if needed (ASAP)
- morgan: schedule postmortem meeting and own RCA write-up (+48h)

eva (sre): running stress harness now. will paste heatmap when done.

ops-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated at 2026-03-15T14:15:00Z by rollback/route pin.

june (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep thread open for RCA items and attach logs/timelines.

rahul (eng-runtime): evidence to include in RCA: kernel selection traces, allocator stats, per-request memory profile, canary vs baseline metric dumps, commit id for canary artifact (commit: a7f9d3e).

morgan (pm): ok. draft RCA outline: timeline -> customer impact -> what changed (diff) -> hypothesis & test results -> root cause -> fix plan -> rollout guardrails.

june (oncall): final quick notes: no data exfil seen, no control-plane compromise, isolated to inference runtime artifact. If we need to revert other rollouts that share kernel toggle, we will.

carla (prodops): reopening support tickets with updated status and ETA for RCA.

rahul (eng-runtime): next steps: revert quantization flag and matmul_fuse off in canary branch, run full regression harness, then re-run canary with staged traffic and longer observation window.

morgan (pm): assigned owners look good. we'll aim to publish initial RCA draft within 48h. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident thread will be archived after RCA published."
